thought_title: Truly Born, Truly Nailed for Us

edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Δοξάζω Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν τὸν θεὸν τὸν οὕτως ὑμᾶς σοφίσαντα: ἐνόησα γὰρ ὑμᾶς κατηρτισμένους ἐν ἀκινήτῳ πίστει, ὥσπερ καθηλωμένους ἐν τῷ σταυρῷ τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ σαρκί τε καὶ πνεύματι καὶ ἡδρασμένους ἐν ἀγάπῃ ἐν τῷ αἵματι Χριστοῦ, πεπληροφορημένους εἰς τὸν κύριον ἡμῶν, ἀληθῶς ὄντα ἐκ γένους Δαυεὶδ κατὰ σάρκα, υἱὸν θεοῦ κατὰ θέλημα καὶ δύναμιν θεοῦ, γεγεννημένον ἀληθῶς ἐκ παρθένου, βεβαπτισμένον ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου, ἵνα πληρωθῇ πᾶσα δικαιοσύνη ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ: [2] ἀληθῶς ἐπὶ Ποντίου Πιλάτου καὶ Ἡρώδου τετράρχου καθηλωμένον ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἐν σαρκί, ἀφ̓ οὖ καρποῦ ἡμεῖς ἀπὸ τοῦ θεομακαρίστου αὐτοῦ πάθους, ἵνα ἄρῃ σύσσημον εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας διὰ τῆς ἀναστάσεως εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους καὶ πιστοὺς αὐτοῦ, εἴτε ἐν Ἰουδαίοις εἴτε ἐν ἔθνεσιν, ἐν ἑνὶ σώματι τῆς ἐκκλησίας αὐτοῦ.
pass_a_gloss: [1] I glorify Jesus Christ, the God who has made you so wise. For I have perceived that you have been made complete in an unmovable faith, as if nailed to the cross of the Lord Jesus Christ in both flesh and spirit, and firmly settled in love by the blood of Christ, fully convinced with regard to our Lord: that he is truly from the family of David according to the flesh, Son of God according to the will and power of God, truly born of a virgin, baptized by John so that all righteousness might be fulfilled by him; [2] truly nailed for us in the flesh under Pontius Pilate and Herod the tetrarch, from which fruit we are, from his God-blessed suffering, so that he might lift up a signal-banner for the ages through the resurrection, for his saints and faithful ones, whether among Jews or among Gentiles, in the one body of his church.
pass_b_english: I give glory to Jesus Christ, the God who has made you this wise. I have seen that you are made complete in a faith that cannot be shaken, as though you were nailed to the cross of the Lord Jesus Christ in flesh and in spirit, and set firm in love by the blood of Christ.

You are fully convinced about our Lord. He is truly of David's line according to the flesh (Romans 1:3), and Son of God by God's will and power. He was truly born of a virgin. He was baptized by John so that all righteousness might be fulfilled by him (Matthew 3:15).

Under Pontius Pilate and Herod the tetrarch he was truly nailed for us in the flesh. We are of that fruit, the fruit of his God-blessed passion. So it was that through his resurrection he might raise a banner for the ages (Isaiah 5:26; Isaiah 49:22) for his saints and his faithful ones, Jews or Gentiles alike, in the one body of his church.

choices.why: The article makes 'God' a title of Jesus Christ himself; Ignatius says this plainly.
rejected: God, even Jesus Christ (softens the predication)
God through Jesus Christ (not in the Greek)

choices.why: Ignatius's anti-docetic hammer; kept at each step of the creed and given short sentences so the repetition lands.
Elliptic: we come from the fruit of the cross, i.e. his passion; kept as a short statement without naming a 'tree' the Greek does not name.
rejected: we are the fruit of the tree (adds tree)
by which we live (adds a claim)

choices.why: LXX Isaiah wording for lifting a signal to the nations; 'banner' is plain and keeps the image.

anf_compare.notes: ANF and this draft agree in substance. ANF's 'God, even Jesus Christ' slightly blurs the article; Greek reads 'Jesus Christ, the God'. ANF 'standard' = our 'banner'.

bible_refs.note: Ek genous David kata sarka echoes Paul's 'of the seed of David according to the flesh'; Romans 1:4 also near ('Son of God in power').
'that all righteousness might be fulfilled' echoes 'to fulfill all righteousness'.
LXX 'lift up a signal (syssemon)' for the nations; Isaiah 62:10 is a further possible source.

review.notes: Paragraph [1] (Smyrnaeans 1, sections [1]–[2]) matches the named locus. 'Δοξάζω Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν τὸν θεὸν τὸν οὕτως ὑμᾶς σοφίσαντα' is kept as a predication of God to Christ in A 'I glorify Jesus Christ, the God who has made you so wise' and B 'I give glory to Jesus Christ, the God who has made you this wise'. 'ἐνόησα γὰρ ὑμᾶς κατηρτισμένους ἐν ἀκινήτῳ πίστει' and the nail/blood/conviction chain stay under the Smyrnaeans, with all three ἀληθῶς kept (David κατὰ σάρκα, virgin birth, nailing ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν under Pilate and Herod). 'ἵνα πληρωθῇ πᾶσα δικαιοσύνη ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ' matches 'fulfilled by him'; B's (Matthew 3:15), (Romans 1:3), and (Isaiah 5:26; Isaiah 49:22) sit on those clauses as the supplied wording notes, not apparatus-only. Ellipsis 'ἀφ̓ οὖ καρποῦ ἡμεῖς ἀπὸ τοῦ θεομακαρίστου αὐτοῦ πάθους' is not expanded with a tree: A 'from which fruit we are, from his God-blessed suffering'; B 'We are of that fruit, the fruit of his God-blessed passion'. 'ἵνα ἄρῃ σύσσημον … διὰ τῆς ἀναστάσεως' keeps he/might and the resurrection as means. Title names the anti-docetic thought. Irregular 'ἀφ̓ οὖ' is disclosed.
